close_reason:
Obviated 2026-05-08 by upstream bw fix shipping in local install.

Background: this ticket proposed an audit-trail breadcrumb that would log every time the activation reflex fired (auto-clean of extensions.worktreeconfig). The observability concern was: if the reflex auto-cleans silently, we have no signal when the upstream issue is finally fixed and the reflex stops being necessary.

Why obviated: bw was rebuilt locally from main on 2026-05-08, including PR #117 (extFilteringStorer). bw is now immune to the worktreeconfig issue regardless of what Claude Code's worktree-creation harness writes. The activation reflex no longer needs to fire — there's nothing to breadcrumb.

The observability-when-stale-reflex-keeps-firing concern is also moot: the reflex itself is now legacy, not a load-bearing automation.

Reference: ariadne-core-workspace/NOTES_bw_v0.12.3_vs_main_2026-05-08.md.
description:
CATO follow-up surfaced during stoa--7kg.1 review of the activation-reflex commit (df826a9).

## Concern

The reflex paragraph in operating-disciplines.md §9 + MAJOR_PLINY.md §9 step 3 says: when bw prime hits the worktreeconfig signature, run the three commands mechanically and don't surface to PRINCIPAL. That's correct for ergonomics — it auto-cleans without burning attention — but it's silent. If anthropics fixes anthropics/claude-code#45645 in a future Claude Code release, the reflex would keep firing on stale config until someone notices, with no audit trail of whether the upstream is still live.

CATO's suggested mitigation: each time the reflex fires, leave a one-line breadcrumb noting "worktreeconfig reflex applied <date>". That gives PRINCIPAL eventual observability.

## Open design questions

1. **Where does the breadcrumb land?** Options:
   - The engagement's coordination ticket (but not every session has one).
   - A dedicated reflex-log ticket (e.g., a long-lived "regression observations" ticket per project).
   - The session's own bw activity (no formal log concept exists today).
   - A file-on-disk breadcrumb under `.claude/` (but that pollutes the worktree).

2. **What's the read-side discipline?** The breadcrumb is only useful if someone reads it — POLYBIUS during a periodic sweep? PRINCIPAL during a retrospective?

3. **Volume vs. signal.** If every fresh worktree fires the reflex (which is the empirical pattern), the breadcrumbs accumulate fast. Does the breadcrumb need a frequency-threshold (e.g., one per project per day) to avoid noise?

## Out of scope

- Re-deriving the reflex itself (already shipped in stoa--7kg.1).
- Filing an upstream issue against anthropics/claude-code (existing #45645 covers it).

## Sequencing

Defer until the reflex has fired enough times that the absence of audit trail becomes observably painful. Not blocking any active arc.

comments.text:
Frequency-signal data point from ariadne PLINY's Batch H run (2026-05-07):

  ~10 worktree creations per engagement at typical Batch-H pacing.

Implication for breadcrumb design: per-firing append-log shape will accumulate ~10 entries/session, scaling to dozens per active day. Design likely wants:

- Dedup by date + workspace (one entry per workspace per day, not per firing).
- OR rolling-window summary (e.g., 'reflex fired N times since YYYY-MM-DD').
- OR explicit threshold ('alert when reflex hasn't fired in N days' as the upstream-fixed signal, rather than logging every firing).

The third shape is interesting because it inverts the question: instead of 'when did the reflex stop firing?' (requires reading all entries to detect absence), it becomes 'how long since last firing?' (a single-field check). Less data, sharper signal.

Source: PLINY surface on stoa--7kg comment thread + Batch H close-out 2026-05-07.

title: Audit-trail breadcrumb when worktreeconfig activation reflex fires
